t: A proposer who had surgery for a benign tumour two weeks ago is asked to re-apply after three months. This underwriting decision is called:
o: Postponement
Standard acceptance
Declinature
Acceptance with lien
e: Postponement defers the decision where the risk cannot presently be assessed but may be insurable later; declinature is a refusal of the risk.

t: Because women on average live longer than men, insurers in India typically price a female life as though she were how many years younger than a male of the same age?
o: About 10 years
About 7 years
About 3 years
About 1 year
e: Most Indian insurers apply a female age set-back of around three years, reflecting lower female mortality at most ages.

t: A proposer is 1.75 m tall and weighs 90 kg. His Body Mass Index (BMI) is approximately:
o: 25.7 kg/m²
27.0 kg/m²
32.1 kg/m²
29.4 kg/m²
e: BMI = weight (kg) / height² (m²) = 90 / (1.75 × 1.75) = 90 / 3.0625 ≈ 29.4, which falls in the overweight range of 25-29.9.

t: Death of both parents before the age of 60 from coronary heart disease is significant to an underwriter mainly because:
o: Coronary heart disease has a strong hereditary component, raising the proposer's own expected mortality
It indicates that the proposer is likely to be over-insured
It proves that the proposer lacks insurable interest
It means the proposer must be rated for occupational hazard
e: Family history is a selection factor because conditions like heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers run in families; it has no bearing on insurable interest or occupation.

t: A proposer declares that he stopped smoking six months ago. Under usual Indian underwriting practice, he would be classified as:
o: A non-smoker, because he is not smoking at the time of proposal
An uninsurable life until he has quit for five years
A smoker, since most insurers require at least 12 months of abstinence for non-smoker rates
A preferred non-smoker, because quitting shows good health awareness
e: Non-smoker rates are usually given only after 12 months of complete abstinence from tobacco in any form; six months is insufficient.

t: The medical examiner who examines a proposer on behalf of the insurer should NOT be:
o: A doctor empanelled by the insurer
A relative of the proposer or the agent who sold the policy
A doctor holding an MBBS qualification
A doctor practising in the proposer's city
e: To preserve independence, the examiner must not have any relationship with the proposer or the intermediary; empanelled, qualified local doctors are expected.

t: A woman in the seventh month of pregnancy with a history of pregnancy-induced hypertension applies for a ₹50 lakh endowment policy. The most appropriate underwriting decision is:
o: Decline permanently because of hypertension
Accept with a permanent flat extra for pregnancy
Postpone the proposal until a few weeks after delivery and normal recovery
Accept at standard rates since pregnancy is a normal condition
e: Complicated pregnancy carries a temporary extra risk; underwriters postpone until after confinement rather than decline or rate permanently.

t: Under current IRDAI product regulations, a lapsed non-linked individual life policy can generally be revived within:
o: 5 years from the date of the first unpaid premium
2 years from the date of the first unpaid premium
10 years from the policy commencement date
1 year from the date of lapse
e: The revival period is 5 years from the first unpaid premium; revival requires payment of arrears with interest and satisfactory evidence of continued insurability.

t: A flat extra premium of ₹3 per thousand sum assured is imposed for occupational hazard on a policy of ₹8 lakh. The annual extra premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Flat extra = ₹3 × (8,00,000 / 1,000) = ₹3 × 800 = ₹2,400 per annum.

t: When a policy is revived with fresh evidence of health, Section 45 provides that:
o: The contestability period is reduced to one year
The 3-year contestability period runs afresh from the date of revival for the revived policy
The policy becomes incontestable immediately on revival
Revival has no effect on contestability
e: Section 45 counts 3 years from the later of issuance, commencement of risk, revival or rider addition, so revival restarts the clock.

t: In group life underwriting, the 'free cover limit' means:
o: The maximum age for joining the scheme
The sum assured up to which each member is covered without individual medical evidence
The amount of premium the employer need not pay
The portion of the group ceded to the reinsurer
e: Above the free cover limit, members must furnish individual evidence of insurability; the limit depends on group size and average cover.

t: A life insurer's underwriting manual is best described as:
o: A company guide listing impairments, required evidence and the ratings to apply, usually developed with reinsurer input
The IRDAI regulation on policy issuance
A list of all policyholders and their sums assured
The agent's commission schedule
e: The manual ensures consistency between underwriters; reinsurers often supply manuals to cedants.

t: Sunil pays an annual premium of ₹60,000 on a policy with a sum assured of ₹5 lakh issued in 2023. The premium eligible for deduction under Section 80C is:
e: Deduction is capped at 10% of sum assured = ₹50,000, as the premium (12% of SA) exceeds the limit.

t: Under Section 10(10D), the maturity proceeds of a non-ULIP life policy issued on or after 1 April 2023 become taxable if the aggregate annual premium exceeds:
o: ₹2.5 lakh
₹10 lakh
₹1.5 lakh
₹5 lakh
e: Finance Act 2023 taxes maturity of high-premium traditional policies (aggregate premium above ₹5 lakh); ULIPs have a ₹2.5 lakh threshold since 2021. Death benefits remain exempt.

t: The premium paid by a company on a keyman insurance policy is generally allowed as a deduction under:
o: Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act
Section 80C of the Income Tax Act
Section 45 of the Insurance Act
Section 37(1) of the Income Tax Act as business expenditure
e: Keyman premium is a business expense under Section 37(1); the claim proceeds received by the company are taxable as business income.

t: As per CBDT and IRDAI guidance, a keyman insurance policy should be:
o: A unit-linked plan
An endowment plan with bonuses
A pure term assurance plan
A whole-life plan with cash value
e: Since 2013, keyman policies must be term plans so that the benefit is purely protection against loss of the key person, not a savings vehicle for the company.

t: A 30-year-old with mild intermittent asthma, using an inhaler occasionally with no hospitalisation, is usually underwritten as:
o: Standard or a small extra
Decline
+200% extra
Postpone until asthma resolves
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Mild, well-controlled asthma carries negligible extra mortality; severe asthma with hospital admissions, steroid dependence or ICU care is rated significantly.

t: A financial questionnaire with supporting documents is most commonly insisted upon when:
o: The proposer is below 25 years of age
The proposer opts for monthly premium mode
The sum assured is large relative to the insurer's limits or the proposal is on the life of another person
The policy term is less than 5 years
e: Large covers and third-party proposals carry the greatest risk of over-insurance and moral hazard, so income and purpose must be documented.

t: For disability and waiver-of-premium riders, occupation is more important than for the death benefit because:
o: Riders are not underwritten
Many occupations carry a high risk of injury or morbidity that does not proportionately affect mortality
Disability riders are sold only to office workers
Occupation does not affect death claims at all
e: Manual and hazardous occupations produce more disability claims; disability underwriting uses occupational classes more strictly than life underwriting.

t: Which of the following is correct about an occupational flat extra premium?
o: It can be charged only on term plans
It is expressed as a percentage of the standard mortality rate
It automatically increases every policy year
It is expressed as a fixed amount per ₹1,000 sum assured and does not vary with the age of the life assured
e: Flat extras are per-mille loadings suited to constant accident hazards; percentage extra mortality ratings are used for medical impairments.

t: Once a life policy without occupational exclusions is issued, a later change to a more hazardous occupation:
o: Automatically voids the policy
Does not affect the policy, as life policies are not conditional on continuance of occupation unless specifically provided
Must be reported within 30 days or the policy lapses
Doubles the premium from the next due date
e: Life insurance covers death from any cause; unlike some accident riders, the base contract is not avoided by a change of occupation.

t: A proposer goes on guided trekking holidays in the Himalayas up to altitudes of 4,000 m twice a year. The usual underwriting view is:
o: Heavy flat extra for the whole term
Decline, as all mountain activities are uninsurable
Postpone until he gives up trekking
Standard, as non-technical trekking at moderate altitude carries little extra mortality
e: Ratings for mountaineering apply to technical climbing, high altitude (typically above 5,000-6,000 m) and expeditions, not ordinary trekking.

t: Apart from risk transfer, life reinsurers typically provide cedants with:
o: Agency recruitment services
Underwriting manuals, training, facultative opinions and product-development support
Policyholder claim settlement on behalf of IRDAI
Guaranteed investment returns
e: Reinsurers' international experience makes them a key source of underwriting expertise for Indian insurers.

t: Under IRDAI (Reinsurance) Regulations, 2018, the obligatory cession to GIC Re applies to:
o: Both life and general insurance equally
General insurance business only, not to life insurance
Life insurance only
Health insurance only
e: Section 101A obligatory cession is prescribed for general insurers; life insurers reinsure under their own board-approved programmes.

t: To be eligible as a cross-border reinsurer (CBR) for Indian insurers, IRDAI requires, among other things:
o: Registration as an Indian company
Approval from the Life Insurance Council
A minimum credit rating (BBB from S&P or equivalent) maintained for at least the past 3 years
A branch in every Indian state
e: CBRs must meet rating, solvency and track-record criteria and are placed after Indian reinsurers and foreign reinsurance branches in the order of preference.

t: The transfer of risk by a reinsurer to another reinsurer is called:
o: Retrocession
Subrogation
Novation
Cession
e: Retrocession spreads the reinsurer's own exposure; cession is the original transfer from insurer to reinsurer.

t: A 32-year-old was treated for Hodgkin's lymphoma five years ago and is in complete remission. The usual underwriting approach is:
o: Decline permanently as lymphoma always recurs
Standard without any evidence
Postpone for a further 20 years
Accept with a temporary extra that reduces over time, as Hodgkin's disease has a good long-term prognosis after treatment
e: Hodgkin's lymphoma has high cure rates; ratings depend on stage, time since treatment and absence of relapse, falling to standard after several years.

t: Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is a disorder in which:
o: The blood clots too readily
The haemoglobin is abnormally high
The white cell count is zero
The platelet count is reduced, leading to bruising and bleeding
e: ITP is immune-mediated platelet destruction; underwriting depends on platelet count, bleeding episodes and treatment (steroids, splenectomy).

t: A 30-year-old proposer earns ₹8 lakh per annum. If the insurer's financial guideline allows 20 times annual income at this age, the maximum total life cover justified is:
o: ₹2.4 crore
₹16 lakh
₹80 lakh
₹1.6 crore
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Maximum cover = 20 × ₹8 lakh = ₹1.6 crore, inclusive of existing policies with all insurers.

t: A transient ischaemic attack (TIA) is significant to the underwriter because:
o: It is a warning sign of an impending stroke caused by temporary reduction in blood supply to the brain
It indicates a benign brain tumour
It is a form of migraine with no mortality implications
It only occurs in people under 20
e: TIAs resolve within 24 hours but signal cerebrovascular disease; they are rated similarly to minor strokes with attention to risk factors.

t: Multiple sclerosis is best described as:
o: A hereditary bleeding disorder
An acute bacterial infection of the brain coverings
A chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, often relapsing and remitting
A form of epilepsy
e: Underwriting depends on the pattern (relapsing-remitting vs progressive), disability level and time since diagnosis; advanced cases are declined.

t: Which combination of factors would lead to the heaviest rating for a diabetic proposer?
o: Onset after 60, short duration and good control
Diet-controlled diabetes with normal HbA1c
Young age at onset, long duration, poor control and presence of complications
Gestational diabetes that resolved after delivery
e: Mortality in diabetes rises with duration, early onset, HbA1c level and complications; co-morbid hypertension, obesity and smoking add further debits.

t: A 50-year-old Type 2 diabetic for 3 years on metformin has HbA1c 6.8%, BMI 26, normal BP and no complications. The most likely underwriting decision is:
o: Postpone until HbA1c falls below 5%
Accept with a modest extra mortality rating (e.g., +50% to +100%)
Standard, as the diabetes is well controlled
Decline, as all diabetics are uninsurable
e: Well-controlled, uncomplicated late-onset Type 2 diabetes carries moderate extra mortality; it is insurable at a mild to moderate rating, not standard.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
o: Insurance Act 1938
IRDA Act 1999
General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972
LIC Act 1956
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: A diabetic proposer has HbA1c of 10.5% and is found to have proliferative retinopathy. The appropriate decision is:
o: Standard with an exclusion for eye disease
Accept at +25%
Accept only under the non-medical scheme
Heavy rating or declinature, as poor control with established microvascular complications indicates high mortality
e: Proliferative retinopathy signals advanced disease that usually coexists with nephropathy and cardiovascular risk; such cases are often declined.

t: A solitary thyroid nodule found on examination of a proposer should be evaluated by:
o: A treadmill test
Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) and ultrasound to exclude malignancy
A chest X-ray only
Urine routine examination
e: Most nodules are benign, but FNAC is needed to exclude thyroid cancer before the underwriter can treat the nodule as benign.

t: Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid treated by total thyroidectomy with no spread is generally:
o: Insurable with a modest temporary extra, as it has an excellent long-term prognosis
Declined permanently like all cancers
Standard immediately after surgery without any evidence
Postponed for 20 years
e: Papillary and follicular thyroid cancers have very high survival; anaplastic carcinoma, in contrast, is almost always declined.

t: Nephrotic syndrome is characterised by:
o: Painless haematuria only
Kidney stones and renal colic
Heavy proteinuria, low serum albumin and oedema
High blood sugar and glycosuria
e: Nephrotic syndrome reflects significant glomerular disease; underwriting depends on the cause, response to treatment and renal function.

t: A proposer passed a single kidney stone three years ago, with no recurrence and normal renal function. The usual decision is:
o: +100% extra
Standard
Postpone for five years
Decline
e: An isolated stone episode has no mortality significance; recurrent stones, obstruction or impaired function require further assessment.

t: Pleural effusion found on a chest X-ray is underwritten according to:
o: Its underlying cause, such as tuberculosis, heart failure or malignancy
The proposer's blood group
The number of cigarettes smoked that day
The size of the X-ray film
e: Fluid in the pleural space is a sign, not a diagnosis; a resolved tuberculous effusion may be standard while a malignant effusion is declined.

t: Obstructive sleep apnoea is relevant to life underwriting because:
o: It is associated with obesity, hypertension, cardiovascular disease and daytime sleepiness causing accidents
It is a form of lung cancer
It occurs only in children
It indicates excellent cardiovascular fitness
e: Untreated moderate to severe sleep apnoea is rated; good compliance with CPAP therapy and control of risk factors improves the terms.

t: Established cirrhosis of the liver is usually underwritten as:
o: +50% extra
Lien for 3 years
Decline
Standard
e: Cirrhosis is irreversible with high mortality from liver failure, bleeding varices and hepatocellular carcinoma.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
o: ₹50 crore
₹100 crore
₹200 crore
₹500 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) found on ultrasound with normal liver enzymes in an overweight proposer is usually:
o: Declined because it leads to cirrhosis in all cases
Rated for the build and any associated diabetes or lipids, with the fatty liver itself not attracting a separate heavy rating
Postponed for 5 years
Accepted only with an exclusion of liver disease
e: Simple fatty liver is common with metabolic risk factors; raised enzymes (steatohepatitis) or fibrosis warrant additional rating.

t: Mitral stenosis in India is most commonly a consequence of:
o: Hypertension
Smoking
Diabetes
Rheumatic heart disease
e: Rheumatic fever damages heart valves, particularly the mitral valve; severity, atrial fibrillation and heart failure determine the rating.

t: A proposer had an atrial septal defect (ASD) surgically closed in childhood and has a normal echocardiogram now. The usual decision is:
o: Decline
+200% extra
Standard
Postpone until age 40
e: A repaired simple congenital defect with normal cardiac function carries no extra mortality; unrepaired defects with pulmonary hypertension are declined.

t: The investigation that best distinguishes an innocent (functional) heart murmur from an organic one is:
o: Echocardiography
Chest X-ray
Urine examination
Blood sugar test
e: Echo shows valve structure and function; innocent murmurs with normal echo are standard.

t: Atrial fibrillation is a concern for life underwriters mainly because:
o: It is a sign of thyroid underactivity only
It always indicates lung cancer
It increases the risk of stroke from embolism and may indicate underlying heart disease
It has no effect on mortality
e: AF requires assessment of the cause (valvular disease, hypertension, thyrotoxicosis), rate control and anticoagulation.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Recurrent uveitis in a proposer is significant mainly because:
o: It indicates diabetes in all cases
It is caused by loud noise
It always leads to death within a year
It may be a manifestation of systemic disease such as tuberculosis, sarcoidosis or ankylosing spondylitis
e: Uveitis is inflammation of the uveal tract; the underwriter seeks the underlying cause, which determines the rating.

topic: Special Senses: Disorders of the Eyes, Ears and Nose
t: Otosclerosis causes:
o: Progressive conductive hearing loss due to fixation of the stapes, with no mortality significance
Chronic kidney disease
Vertigo with vomiting
Sudden blindness
e: Otosclerosis is a benign ear condition, often corrected surgically; it is standard for life cover.
